constraints: Work events are protected by the work_hours hard constraint and are left unchanged.
The Wednesday university assessment is protected by the exam_protection hard constraint and is left unchanged.
All proposed preparation time stays within the 08:00–23:00 local daily scheduling bounds.
Times use the Europe/Lisbon timezone offset applicable on these dates, +00:00.
priorities: The user requested at least three hours of preparation for Wednesday's assessment, so the proposal creates exactly three hours across Monday and Tuesday evenings.
Assessment preparation has high priority and is scheduled outside working hours.
Existing gym sessions are preserved because there is enough evening availability after gym without moving flexible events.
Study blocks end before 22:30, matching the preference for evening study to finish by then.

alternatives_considered.option: Schedule one three-hour preparation block on Monday from 20:00 to 23:00.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It would meet the hard daily bound but would end later than the preferred 22:30 study finish time and concentrate all preparation on one evening.

alternatives_considered.option: Move one or both gym sessions to create earlier evening study time.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Gym is flexible, but moving it is unnecessary because the required three hours can be added after the existing gym sessions while respecting all constraints.

alternatives_considered.option: Add preparation before work on Monday or Tuesday.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The user specifically asked to reorganize Monday and Tuesday evenings, and evening slots are available.

rationale.summary: Adds two assessment preparation blocks, 20:00–21:30 on Monday and Tuesday, giving the requested three hours while leaving protected work and exam events unchanged and preserving both gym sessions.

weaknesses: Several claims depend on unseen calendar facts, such as existing work events, gym sessions, and the Wednesday assessment; these cannot be independently verified from the proposal alone.
The rationale says preparation is scheduled after existing gym sessions, but the proposal does not include the gym event times, so that trade-off is not fully supported by the provided evidence.
The proposal assumes Monday and Tuesday evenings are available aside from preserved events, but no availability view or conflict check is shown.
The hard constraints are stated clearly, but the proposal does not show how each proposed block was checked against all existing events, only that protected events are left unchanged.
The alternatives are plausible, but their rejection partly relies on unverified details about available evening slots and gym flexibility.
critic_evaluation.feedback: The proposal is internally mostly coherent: two 90-minute blocks produce exactly three hours, both end before 22:30, and the rejected single 20:00–23:00 block is consistently described as worse under the stated preference. To strengthen the rationale, include the relevant existing Monday and Tuesday evening calendar context, especially work, gym, and any other events, so the claim that 20:00–21:30 is available can be assessed. Also make explicit whether the Wednesday assessment date is indeed the relevant protected event and whether these blocks are close enough to it to satisfy the preparation goal. The alternatives section is useful, but it would be stronger if each rejection were tied to visible schedule evidence rather than asserted availability.
